sentences.vi: whereas / while nối hai vế đối lập trong một câu. Unlike / Compared with đứng đầu câu rồi có phẩy. Although + mệnh đề (nhượng bộ); because of + danh từ.
sentences.exampleEn: Online lessons can be replayed, whereas classroom explanations are heard only once. Unlike a video, a teacher can answer questions at once.

ideas.vi: Chọn MỘT tiêu chí so sánh làm Claim: giáo viên nhận ra học sinh cần giúp dễ hay khó. Ý hay nhưng khác tiêu chí thì không dùng.
ideas.exampleEn: Claim: noticing who needs help → How: see confused faces at a glance → Example: Ms Mai walks between the tables → Result: help before the student asks

write.vi: Mỗi ý so sánh đủ hai bên. Cần whereas / while và Unlike / Compared with, cộng một mệnh đề nhượng bộ. However đứng đầu câu mới.
write.exampleEn: Compared with a classroom, an online lesson makes it harder for a teacher to notice a silent student, although chat tools can help.

recall.vi: can / may / tend to làm nhận định mềm. should / should not nêu lập trường. must not ≠ don't have to.
recall.exampleEn: Students don't have to work part-time, but those who do tend to become more responsible.

write.prompt: Compare online and classroom lessons in terms of how easily a teacher can notice a student who needs help. Which works better for secondary school students? Write a paragraph.
write.taskVi: đoạn 110–130 từ (mở rộng: 140–160 từ, không khung): một tiêu chí, so sánh trực tiếp, giải thích, ví dụ, đánh giá.
mustUse: whereas / while và Unlike / Compared with
write.modelAfterSubmit: When it comes to noticing students who need help, classroom lessons are more effective than live online classes. In a classroom, a teacher can walk between the tables and see at a glance which students look confused, whereas in an online class she often sees only rows of small video boxes. Unlike a classroom teacher, who can see every face at once, an online teacher may not notice a student who has turned off the camera. For example, during our online speaking lessons, Ms Mai could visit only one breakout room at a time, so some pairs waited a long time for help. Although online platforms have chat and hand-raising tools, shy students rarely use them. Therefore, secondary students, who still need close support, benefit more from face-to-face lessons.
